story: Completing the second token of a multi-token British proper name (Covent Garden, Notting Hill, Sweeney Todd, Tudor), where the first name-fragment strongly implies the rest.
Predicting the connective or punctuation that glues guidebook prose and listings together — 'and', 'of', a comma, or the next chunk of a time like '4.30'.
Completing prices and opening hours: the digits after a decimal point or pound sign (£16.[50]) and 'am' after a clock number.
Predicting the formatting tokens inside listing lines: the double-space spacer after a semicolon, and the day abbreviations or closing brackets in opening-hours strings.
Predicting the extra whitespace token inside the '(  MAP   GOOGLE MAP )' listing boilerplate, plus similar spacer/continuation tokens after commas and brackets late in a listing.
Reproducing the '(  MAP   GOOGLE MAP ) ;  %phone' boilerplate that repeats verbatim in every guidebook entry — predicting ' MAP', ' %', ' G' at the same spots it appeared before.
Completing the second half of an uncommon word or name that was split across tokens (Wand-ering, Dunk-irk, Pri-ory, MUSE-UM), from lexical knowledge rather than copying.
Continuing URLs and repeated web/boilerplate strings — the dot after 'www', the 'uk' after '.co', 'LE' after 'GOOG' — copying patterns already seen in the passage.
Predicting the next ordinary function word ('the', 'a', 'you', 'right') in flowing descriptive prose, typically right after a connective or preposition.
Predicting the punctuation or short linking word that closes off a noun phrase mid-sentence — a comma, period, 'as', 'and', or 'the' right after a content word.
Early-layer prediction of listing-detail tokens: 'pm'/'am' after a clock number, and the comma or semicolon after a street name like 'Tooley St'.
Finishing a word fragment into a full word, often around a hyphen (triple-gl-azed, flip-fl-ops, sunn-iest, pick-les), or the noun completing a set phrase.
Predicting the full stop that ends a long descriptive sentence, right after its final noun (…as a museum in 1925[.], …from the tourist office[.]).
Predicting the pound sign in price listings ('adult/child £', 'r from £', 'mains £') and the stock phrase ending 'bookings are essential'.
Predicting the period that closes a sentence whose last word is a place or scene noun (…the South Downs National Park[.], …the River Thames[.]).
Predicting the closing parenthesis of the '(  MAP   GOOGLE MAP )' boilerplate and similar bracket-closing tokens at the end of listing parentheticals.
Predicting the newline after a sentence-final period at the end of a paragraph (…make transport a breeze.[\n]).
Completing a well-known collocation or split word from world knowledge — 'Great Hall', 'official London residence', 'dreaming spires', 'bus-kers'.
Predicting the possessive/contraction "'s" after a noun or 'There' (There['s], England['s], the world['s]).
